chapter: Jazz club letters and Dr. Sushan
title: La Rocca on Sushan speaking from both sides and the Averty correspondence
summary: La Rocca calls Sushan two-faced for later backing Tom Brown, and introduces the French correspondent Averty and a letter he wants read.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Managers, bookers and the business of getting work

blocks.x: Well, that'll go to show you how a man can speak out of both sides of his mouth. I received a letter. Now, there's been plenty going on after Marshall Steins had given Tom Brown this favorable write-up. Brown was to go to different papers and have this printed and show it as real history. This was lying history connived by this man, Marshall Steins, who somewhere along in the front of these reels, you'll read his letter that he admitted to me he was lying. Now, they come up with more lies. There's a man from France, Mr. Avedy is his name. He wrote Howard Jacobs and asked him and sent an article in the paper that he would like to reach some old jazz man. I was one of the men that corresponded with him. I think Tom Brown may have had because he's got some of Tom Brown's stuff in there. And he may have contacted this fellow, Morez and Walter Cotfield. Would you read this letter here?
Yeah, I think it should be. It may take a little longer.
Yeah, that's all right. Well, I guess we're about to take. It'll run out, but that's all right.

This letter he is about to read now. I've come across it by accident. It will show a man how he spoke out of both sides of his mouth. 1949, he said that there was no other band. Now he's promoting Tom Brown, who is recording and who is a member, and got 30 pieces of silver in the form of a loving cup, like Judas Iscariot got when he sold Christ. Would you please read that article from Mr. Sushant?
